slides.title: Why churn is rising
The churn rise is an SMB problem: mid-market rose slightly and enterprise did not move

claims.claim: The rise is concentrated in the self-serve segment
evidence: Monthly logo churn H1 2025 → H1 2026: SMB 2.0% → 3.1%; Mid-market 0.6% → 0.8%; Enterprise 0.2% → 0.2%
55% relative rise in SMB monthly logo churn in a year

claims.claim: SMB: holds most of the customers but less than a quarter of ARR, and carries almost all of the rise
Mid-market: a small rise from a low base, with no exit reasons in the pack; worth watching at renewal
Enterprise: unchanged, held in place by multi-year contracts
The board dashboard's "monthly churn 1.4% → 2.3%" has no definition and matches neither a customer- nor an ARR-weighted average of these segments

slides.title: The 2025 promotion cohort drives about 94% of the SMB churn rise; other SMB customers barely moved

claims.claim: One cohort, not the whole segment, moved
evidence: 94.1% of the rise in SMB monthly churn comes from the promotion cohort
Bridge: SMB churn H1 2025 2.0%; customers not from the promotion +0.0644 pp; 2025 promotion cohort +1.0356 pp; SMB churn H1 2026 3.1%

claims.claim: Promotion cohort: 2,100 customers churning at an implied 4.9% a month
evidence: Each group is weighted by its mid-2026 customer count (3,800 not from the promotion, 2,100 from it); the cohort's rate is implied from Table 1, not reported
The cohort is compared with the 2.0% monthly churn of similar SMB customers in H1 2025

claims.claim: Other SMB: up a tenth of a percentage point, despite Inkwell

slides.title: Promotion customers never got started and left when the discount ended, while other customers' price complaints held steady

claims.claim: Only 41% of promotion customers got started, compared with 72% of other new customers
evidence: Sent five or more documents in month one: Promotion cohort 41%; Other cohorts 72%
SMB customers who send fewer than five documents in their first month churn at about three times the rate of those who send more

claims.claim: Price complaints rose only among promotion leavers; other SMB leavers cite price as often as in 2025
evidence: SMB churners citing price: Promotion cohort H1 2026 52%; All SMB H1 2026 34%; All SMB H1 2025 19%; Not from the promotion H1 2026 18%

claims.claim: The cohort reacted to its price doubling; a list-price rise on top would hit the group likeliest to leave
evidence: Most promotion-cohort customers who left did so within two months of the discount ending; the promotion gave 50% off for the first six months, February to August 2025

slides.title: Onboarding alone can remove about a tenth of SMB churn; most of the promotion's damage was a one-off discount cliff

claims.claim: The halving Customer Success expects is out of reach
evidence: SMB monthly churn: H1 2026 3.1%; once the discount cliff has passed 2.3971%; if the cohort also gets started 2.1%
Customer Success target: halve it 1.6%

claims.claim: Discount cliff: most promotion leavers went within two months of the discount ending; this part should fade on its own
Onboarding: a 72% start rate, as in other cohorts, removes the rest of the cohort's excess
evidence: Promotion cohort churn H1 2026 4.9% − one-off discount cliff 2.9% = explained by its low start rate 1.97%
Share of SMB churn onboarding alone can remove 9.6% (0.3 pp ÷ 3.1%)

claims.claim: Floor: SMB churn then sits at the rate of customers not from the promotion

slides.title: Where Palisade has pricing power
Pricing power sits in mid-market and enterprise, where customers expand, stay and rarely meet Inkwell

claims.claim: Mid-market: Largest prize / Almost half of all ARR, and most of it renews in 2027
evidence: NRR 112%; monthly logo churn 0.8%; 85% of ARR renewing in 2027; Integrations and audit trail; Inkwell not seen in deals above 200 seats

claims.claim: Enterprise: Strong, but capped and mostly not renewing
evidence: NRR 118%; monthly logo churn 0.2%; 40% of ARR renewing in 2027; Integrations and audit trail; 60% of ARR capped at 7% a year

claims.claim: SMB: Unproven: test before raising
evidence: NRR 94%; monthly logo churn 3.1%; all ARR renewing in 2027; Inkwell Starter at $9 against our $15; win rate against it down to 38%

claims.claim: mid-market churn did rise from 0.6% to 0.8% a month, and the pack has no mid-market exit reasons

slides.title: Inkwell's $9 plan undercuts our SMB price by 40%, and we now lose most SMB deals where it competes

claims.claim: Inkwell's Starter plan costs 40% less than the Palisade SMB plan
evidence: List price $/user/month from October 2025: Inkwell Starter 9; Palisade SMB 15; Inkwell Pro 24; Palisade Business 29

claims.claim: Our SMB win rate where Inkwell competes fell to 38% within a year of its launch
evidence: −13 pp

claims.claim: Inkwell has not appeared in mid-market or enterprise deals above 200 seats; the threat is confined to SMB for now
evidence: Smaller mid-market deals of up to 200 seats may still meet Inkwell; the pack does not split mid-market renewals by seat count

slides.title: Our own price history says mid-market barely reacts to a rise and SMB churn recovers within six months

claims.claim: After the 8% SMB rise in 2023, churn jumped for six months, then settled near its old level
evidence: SMB churn: before the rise 1.8%; first six months 2.3%; after it settled 1.9%

claims.claim: A 10% higher list price did not measurably change mid-market conversion in 2024
evidence: Conversion: control price 23.6%; 10% higher list price 23.1%
the conversion gap was not statistically significant

claims.claim: Both are imperfect guides: the 2023 rise came before Inkwell's $9 plan, and the 2024 test covered new sign-ups for three months, not renewals

slides.title: The CFO's proposal
The CFO's plan is worth about $7.6M in 2027, not $10.3M, once renewal dates and price caps apply

claims.claim: The CFO's plan is worth about $7.6M in 2027, not $10.3M
evidence: CFO headline 12% on all ARR $10.3M; ARR not renewing in 2027 −$2.466M; Enterprise price caps −$0.288M; Reachable in 2027 $7.566M
the headline of $10.3M is 12% of all $86.0M ARR

claims.claim: A third of what is left rests on the riskiest segment
evidence: 33.3% of the reachable gain would come from SMB, where churn is rising

claims.claim: Not renewing: 60% of enterprise and 15% of mid-market ARR keeps today's terms
Price caps: capped contracts rise 7% at most

slides.title: A segmented plan keeps most of the CFO's reachable gain while sparing the customers most likely to leave

claims.claim: Hold all prices — Rejected: churn rise is not a core price problem
evidence: ARR gain: None; No one, but the strongest segments are left unpriced; Relies entirely on retention and new customers

claims.claim: CFO: 12% on every plan — Rejected: a third of the gain rests on SMB
evidence: $7.6M; Promotion cohort and SMB customers facing Inkwell; Largest on paper; SMB churn response untested at 12%

claims.claim: Segmented, SMB step staged — Recommended / Most of the CFO's gain, with SMB tested before it scales
evidence: $5.6M; Mostly mid-market and enterprise; SMB behind a stop rule; About level with it before new customers

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise only — Fallback if the SMB stop rule triggers
evidence: $4.3M; Only the segments with proven retention; Slightly short before new customers

slides.title: The segmented plan and its rollout
The segmented plan still adds about $5.6M; most of what it gives up is SMB revenue at risk of churning

claims.claim: The segmented plan still adds about $5.6M
evidence: Reachable under the CFO plan $7.566M; Promotion cohort price held −$0.528M; Other SMB 8% not 12% −$0.664M; Mid-market 10% not 12% −$0.697M; Enterprise uncapped 10% not 12% −$0.0768M; Segmented plan $5.6002M
Plan gain = mid-market $41.0M × 85% renewing × 10% + enterprise $24.0M × 40% × (60% × 7% + 40% × 10%) + other SMB $16.6M × 8%

claims.claim: We give up gain where churn risk is highest
evidence: 60.6% of the gain given up against the CFO plan is SMB revenue

claims.claim: Promotion cohort: price held while it gets started; Other SMB: repeats the 2023 step of 8%, whose effect we know; Mid-market: the 10% tested in 2024
Mid-market and enterprise carry most of the gain
Not included: if multi-year enterprise contracts allow a 7% escalator before renewal, up to about $1.0M more; the pack does not say

slides.title: Even if churn reacts only as it did in 2023, the 8% SMB step nets just about $0.7M

claims.claim: the 8% SMB step nets just about $0.7M
evidence: $16.6M ARR of SMB customers not from the promotion, all renewing in 2027 × 8% price step − $0.6M ARR lost if churn reacts as in 2023 (+0.5 pp for six months, then +0.1 pp) = $0.7M net gain in 2027, about half the gross gain

claims.claim: The step is small and close to break-even, so it needs a stop rule
evidence: Break-even: the step stops paying if it lifts monthly SMB churn by more than about 0.6 percentage points through 2027 (8% ÷ 108% ÷ 12 months)

slides.title: On today's retention, the plan grows ARR about 15% before any new customers: level with the objective, with no cushion

claims.claim: the plan grows ARR about 15% before any new customers
evidence: ARR mid-2026 $86M; existing customers at today's retention +$7.98M; price plan, net of SMB churn +$4.95479M; ARR end-2027 $98.9348M
$86M × 109.3% net revenue retention + $4.95M price plan, net = $98.9M
ARR growth from existing customers 15.04% ($98.9M ÷ $86.0M − 1)
Net revenue retention with the plan 115.04%
Range before new customers: $98.25M (14.2%) if the SMB step is stopped, $99.6M if it causes no churn response

claims.claim: Both objectives are met only if mid-market renewals hold
Retention: the biggest step, if each segment holds
Risk: a mid-market churn response puts 15% out of reach
new-customer ARR, not in the pack, is the only cushion

slides.title: Mid-market and enterprise move from January, while the SMB step waits for a one-quarter test

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise move from January, while the SMB step waits for a one-quarter test
evidence: Leadership: Approve plan and stop rules (Dec 2026)
Mid-market: 10% at renewal; New price on every 2027 renewal
Enterprise: up to cap; 7% capped, 10% uncapped, at renewal
Other SMB: 8% step; Test on half; SMB go / no-go; Roll out if the stop rule holds; Six-month SMB check
Promotion cohort: Activation drive, price held; Review price with activation data
New SMB sign-ups: List price stays at $15 while Inkwell undercuts
The test randomly assigns half of the renewing SMB customers not from the promotion to the 8% step and keeps the other half as control

claims.claim: Decision for December: approve the segmented plan with its stop rules, not a single 12% rise

slides.title: Five measures, each with a stop level, tell leadership within a quarter whether to pause a step

claims.claim: Five measures, each with a stop level, tell leadership within a quarter whether to pause a step
evidence: SMB test group extra monthly churn over control: today Test starts in January; stop 0.5 pp; Stop the step; hold SMB prices for 2027; Above 2023's jump means worse than 2023
Mid-market monthly logo churn: 0.8%; stop 1.6%; Pause further rises; review 51–200-seat accounts first; Break-even of the 10% step
Overall net revenue retention: 109.3%; stop 100%; Revisit every step; Company objective
Promotion cohort share getting started: 41%; 72%; Below it by Q3: accept the churn, no new discount; Target, not a stop level
SMB win rate where Inkwell competes: 38%; Any further fall; Review the SMB entry offer against Inkwell; Guards new-customer growth

claims.claim: One owner per measure, reviewed monthly; the SMB decision is made in April on the first quarter of test data
evidence: With about 1,900 customers in each SMB test group, a quarter shows a jump the size of 2023's; the six-month check shows whether it settles
Mid-market stop level: 0.8% today plus 0.76 percentage points, the extra churn at which 10% ÷ 110% of renewing ARR is lost over 12 months

slides.title: Appendix
BACKUP: The board dashboard's churn figure matches neither a customer- nor an ARR-weighted view of the segments

claims.claim: The board dashboard's churn figure matches neither a customer- nor an ARR-weighted view of the segments
evidence: Board dashboard, measure not defined: 1.4% → 2.3%; Periods and weighting not stated
Segments weighted by customers: 1.7% → 2.6%; Same size of rise, from a higher base
Segments weighted by ARR: 0.8% → 1.2%; Lower: large accounts churn least
Weighted with mid-2026 customer counts and ARR from Table 1; the dashboard's periods are assumed to match H1 2025 and H1 2026

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Raise 2027 prices in mid-market and enterprise, stage SMB behind a stop rule, spare promotion customers. Decision for December: approve the segmented plan with its stop rules, not a single 12% rise (mid-market 10% at renewal; enterprise 7% capped, 10% uncapped; other SMB 8% step tested on half first; promotion cohort price held with an activation drive; new SMB list price stays at $15).

alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: churn rise is not a core price problem. ARR gain none; strongest segments left unpriced; relies entirely on retention and new customers.
Rejected: a third of the gain rests on SMB. Worth about $7.6M in 2027, not $10.3M, once renewal dates and price caps apply; SMB churn response untested at 12%.
Recommended: most of the CFO's gain ($5.6M), with SMB tested before it scales; about level with the 15% objective before new customers.
Fallback if the SMB stop rule triggers: $4.3M; slightly short of the objective before new customers.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Synthetic benchmark data; every number from the briefing pack
The board dashboard's "monthly churn 1.4% → 2.3%" has no definition; the dashboard's periods are assumed to match H1 2025 and H1 2026
The promotion cohort's churn rate is implied from Table 1, not reported; groups weighted by mid-2026 customer counts
Onboarding estimate assumes non-starters churn about three times as often as starters in both groups; H2 2026 cohort data would confirm that the cliff has passed
Mid-market churn rose from 0.6% to 0.8% and the pack has no mid-market exit reasons
Smaller mid-market deals of up to 200 seats may still meet Inkwell; the pack does not split mid-market renewals by seat count

Both price-history guides are imperfect: the 2023 rise came before Inkwell's $9 plan, and the 2024 test covered new sign-ups for three months, not renewals; the conversion gap was not statistically significant
Assumes capped and uncapped enterprise contracts renew in proportion
Gains are ARR at renewal before any churn response
If multi-year enterprise contracts allow a 7% escalator before renewal, up to about $1.0M more; the pack does not say
Customers not from the promotion react as all SMB did in 2023; Inkwell's $9 plan did not exist then, so the response could be larger
Lost customers are valued at the new price; any effect on new-customer win rates is not included
The 8% SMB step is close to break-even: stops paying if it lifts monthly SMB churn by more than about 0.6 pp through 2027
15% growth is met with no cushion; a mid-market churn response puts 15% out of reach; new-customer ARR, not in the pack, is the only cushion
Range before new customers: $98.25M (14.2%) if the SMB step is stopped, $99.6M if it causes no churn response
next_steps: Approve the segmented 2027 price plan and its stop rules — CEO and leadership team — Dec 2026
Pull H2 2026 SMB churn by cohort to confirm the discount cliff has passed — Finance and Customer Success — Dec 2026
Set up the randomized SMB renewal test and the promotion-cohort activation drive — Growth and Customer Success — Jan 2027
Check which multi-year enterprise contracts allow a 2027 escalator before renewal — Legal and Finance — Q1 2027
Define the board dashboard's churn measure and restate it by segment — CFO — Jan 2027
normalized.extraction_notes: The deck had no images; all charts came through as native chart data. I turned chart values given as fractions into percentages (for example 0.031 became 3.1%) and kept the bridge values at the precision the data shows. On slide 7 the calculation layout (4.9% − 2.9% = 1.97%) was rebuilt from loose labels and operators that arrived out of order. On slide 19 the timeline's mapping of cells to quarters is unclear apart from the stated text (Dec 2026 approval, January start, April SMB decision). The "SECTION" labels, the page and section-number markers, and the navigation strip on each slide were left out.
